title_en: Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. v. Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a financial leasing contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 16 of the Company Law, when a company provides a guarantee for another person's debt, different resolution authorities and resolution procedures apply depending on whether the guaranteed person is a shareholder, actual controller, or other person of the company. If among the guaranteed persons there are both shareholders/actual controllers and persons other than shareholders or actual controllers, and if the guaranteed debt is a joint and several common debt, the guarantee act for the other persons shall be reviewed in accordance with the procedural standards for guarantees provided by the company for its shareholders. The procedural review standards shall not be lowered because one of the joint and several debtors is not a company shareholder.

full_text_en:
Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. v. Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over financial leasing contract

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 16 of the Company Law of the PRC, where a company provides a guarantee for the debts of another person, different resolution authorities and resolution procedures shall apply depending on whether the guaranteed person is a shareholder or de facto controller of the company, or a person other than a shareholder or de facto controller. Where the guaranteed persons include both shareholders or de facto controllers of the company and other persons who are not shareholders or de facto controllers, and if the guaranteed debts are joint and several debts, the guarantee provided to such other persons shall be examined in accordance with the procedural standards applicable to a company providing a guarantee for its shareholders; the procedural examination standard shall not be lowered merely because one joint and several debtor is not a shareholder of the company.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2021) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 232

Re-applicant (Defendant at first instance, Appellant at second instance): Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. XX, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Huang Bo, Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tong Guomin, lawyer of Beijing Bendu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yijia, lawyer of Beijing Bendu Law Firm.

Re-applicant (Defendant at first instance, Appellant at second instance): Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. XX, Hanyang District, Wuhan, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Zhan Guang, Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tong Guomin, lawyer of Beijing Bendu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yijia, lawyer of Beijing Bendu Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at first instance, Appellee at second instance): Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd., domiciled at Tianjin Pilot Free Trade Zone (Dongjiang Bonded Port Area), Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Tang Min, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Jing, lawyer of Tianjin Yungong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Meiqi, lawyer of Tianjin Yungong (Beijing) Law Firm.

Defendants at the original trial: Qingdao Zhongtian Asset Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. XX, Shibei District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Deng Tianzhou, Executive Director of the Company.

Defendant at the original trial: Deng Tianzhou, male, born on August 13, 1956, Han nationality, domiciled at No. XX, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Defendant at the original trial: Huang Bo, male, born on September 1, 1970, Han nationality, domiciled at No. XX, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

The re-applicants, Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. (formerly named Changchun Zhongtian Energy Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Changchun Zhongtian Company) and Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wuhan Zhongneng Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court, disagreeing with the Civil Judgment (2020) Jin Min Zhong No. 370 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court in the case of dispute over a financial leasing contract between them, the respondent Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongmin Company), and the defendants at the original trial, Qingdao Zhongtian Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingdao Zhongtian Company), Deng Tianzhou, and Huang Bo. This Court issued a Civil Ruling (2020) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 5135 on December 10, 2020, deciding to retry the case. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. The re-applicants, Changchun Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and the respondent, Zhongmin Company, appeared and participated in the proceedings. The defendants at the original trial, Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Deng Tianzhou, and Huang Bo, were duly summoned by this Court but did not appear. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

In their application for retrial, Changchun Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company requested: 1. To set aside the Civil Judgment (2019) Jin 03 Min Chu No. 148 rendered by the Tianjin Third Intermediate People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2020) Jin Min Zhong No. 370 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court; 2. To remand the case for a new trial or to have the Supreme People's Court retry and amend the judgment; 3. To order Zhongmin Company to bear all litigation costs. Facts and grounds: (1) The original judgment's finding that Zhongmin Company fulfilled its duty of good faith examination when signing the "Repurchase Agreement" lacks evidentiary support; Changchun Zhongtian Company has sufficient evidence to prove that Zhongmin Company was a malicious counterparty. The second-instance judgment had already found that Zhongmin Company did not provide evidence of examining the shareholders' resolution when signing the "Repurchase Agreement," and entering into a guarantee-type contract without examining the shareholders' resolution for related-party guarantees makes it a malicious counterparty. (2) The form of the board resolution submitted by Zhongmin Company at the second instance was inadmissible; Zhongmin Company failed to fulfill its duty of good faith examination. Specific manifestations: The number of directors who signed and approved the board resolution submitted by Zhongmin Company did not reach the statutory quorum; shareholders of the related company being guaranteed participated in the voting; the form of the resolution was ambiguous in nature and authority; only a board resolution was issued for the related-party guarantee; no public announcement or disclosure was made; the resolution was not archived and was suspected of being forged or altered. The original judgment's finding that Changchun Zhongtian Company could obtain ownership of the leased assets after fulfilling the repurchase obligation was erroneous. (3) The original judgment's dismissal of Wuhan Zhongneng Company's appeal lacks evidentiary support. 1. Wuhan Zhongneng Company was not the actual performing entity under the "Financial Leasing Contract." Although Wuhan Zhongneng Company signed and sealed the "Financial Leasing Contract," and pledged and mortgaged related assets and completed registration, it did not actually perform: First, it did not sell the leased equipment to Zhongmin Company, did not receive any payment from Zhongmin Company, did not issue invoices for the equipment sale, and the full price was deposited into Qingdao Zhongtian Company's account; the purchase/sale of the leased assets did not proceed. This proves that the financial leasing contract was in form only and was essentially a loan. Second, Wuhan Zhongneng Company was nominally the lessee but never paid any rent to Zhongmin Company. Therefore, Wuhan Zhongneng Company was not a party to the "Financial Leasing Contract." The original judgment's finding that the contract in question was a financial leasing contract lacks evidentiary support. 2. When signing the "Financial Leasing Contract," Wuhan Zhongneng Company did not follow the deliberation procedures stipulated in its articles of association; its true intent was not legally expressed, rendering the contract void. At the time of signing the contract, Wuhan Zhongneng Company did not go through the approval process of its shareholders' meeting or board of directors as required; it completely followed the instructions of the de facto controller and relevant personnel of the parent company. This was not a lawful expression of the company's true intent, and the contract is void. 3. The second instance focused on examining Wuhan Zhongneng Company's guarantee, deviating from the substantive nature of the case. All of Wuhan Zhongneng Company's activities in the financial leasing were centered around Qingdao Zhongtian Company; the essence was that Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo, for the benefit of their own company, drained the assets of Changchun Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company. Wuhan Zhongneng Company was merely the nominal seller and lessee, and the pledge and mortgage contracts it signed are also void due to the lack of genuine intent.

Zhongmin Company argued in its defense: (1) The signing of the financial leasing contract, mortgage contract, and pledge contract by Wuhan Zhongneng Company reflected its true intent; these contracts are all genuine, lawful, and valid. Wuhan Zhongneng Company should perform its obligations in accordance with the contract terms. (2) The acts of signing the financial leasing contract, mortgage contract, and pledge contract, as well as completing the pledge registration, all reflected Wuhan Zhongneng Company's true intent and were part of its normal business operations. During the second-instance trial, it admitted the authenticity of the contracts; now, in the retrial, it denies that they reflected its true intent, which is a clear violation of the principle of good faith. (3) There are three cases involving the same financial leasing arrangement. Apart from this case, the other two cases were first-instance judgments, after which Changchun Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company filed appeals but later withdrew them. They then filed for retrial with the Tianjin High Court but have consistently failed to pay the relevant litigation fees. This is a clear abuse of procedural rights to evade enforcement. The current retrial application is also a delay tactic aimed at avoiding debts. (4) The "Repurchase Agreement" between Zhongmin Company and Changchun Zhongtian Company is genuine, lawful, and valid. The "Repurchase Agreement" is a conditional sales contract, a new type of innominate contract, distinct from a guarantee contract, and is not subject to the provisions on guarantees. It does not require approval by the board of directors or shareholders' meeting. (5) Alternatively, even if the court considers the repurchase agreement to be a contract with guarantee functions requiring compliance with guarantee-related provisions, given that the lessee, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Changchun Zhongtian Company, the guarantee provided by Changchun Zhongtian Company for its subsidiary's business activities does not require internal resolution procedures. (6) As a further alternative, even if the court finds that the repurchase agreement in this case is a contract with guarantee functions requiring internal resolution procedures, Changchun Zhongtian Company, as a listed company, followed its articles of association and relevant internal rules when signing the repurchase agreement by completing internal board procedures. The board resolution was genuine, lawful, and valid, complying with Changchun Zhongtian Company's authorization requirements for external guarantees. (7) The contracts in this case were signed in June 2016. The "Minutes of the National Conference on Civil and Commercial Trial Work of Courts" was issued in November 2019 and does not classify repurchase agreements in financial leasing contracts as guarantees. Changchun Zhongtian Company, on the one hand, conflates repurchase with external guarantees, and on the other hand, repeatedly uses the "Minutes" to assess past contracts. This is clearly unfair and violates the principle of good faith.

Zhongmin Company's first-instance claims requested: (1) An order directing Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company to pay to Zhongmin Company the overdue rent of RMB 38,918,750 under the "Financial Leasing Contract" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-001), the overdue payment penalty of RMB 3,635,611.88 calculated as of June 26, 2019, and the overdue payment penalty accruing from June 26, 2019, until the date of actual payment (calculated at 0.05% per day on the overdue rent of RMB 38,918,750 based on the actual number of days overdue); (2) An order directing Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company to pay to Zhongmin Company all future rent not yet due under the "Financial Leasing Contract" amounting to RMB 84,702,500, and the overdue payment penalty (calculated at 0.05% per day on the total future rent of RMB 84,702,500 from the date of filing until the date of actual payment); (3) An order directing Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company to pay to Zhongmin Company damages of RMB 800,000 (calculated at 1% of the principal portion of the future rent under the "Financial Leasing Contract"); (4) An order directing Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company to pay to Zhongmin Company legal fees of RMB 200,000; (The above amounts total a provisional sum of RMB 128,256,861.88.) (5) An order directing Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo to bear joint and several liability for all of the above debts of Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company; (6) An order directing that Zhongmin Company is entitled to priority in satisfaction from the proceeds of the real estate held by Wuhan Zhongneng Company (as detailed in Appendix 1, List of Mortgaged Assets) under the "Mortgage Contract" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-DY) after discount, auction, or sale; (7) An order directing that Zhongmin Company is entitled to priority in satisfaction from the gas operation license right owned by Wuhan Zhongneng Company under the "Pledge Contract" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-ZY); (8) An order directing Changchun Zhongtian Company to perform the repurchase obligation for all of the above claims of Zhongmin Company against Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company under the "Financial Leasing Contract," i.e., to pay the repurchase price to Zhongmin Company equal to the total amount claimed in items (1), (2), (3), (4), and (9); and (9) All litigation costs, preservation fees, etc., shall be borne by Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, Changchun Zhongtian Company, Deng Tianzhou, and Huang Bo.

After trial, the court of first instance found the following facts: On June 22, 2016, the lessor Zhongmin Company and the lessees Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company entered into a "Financial Leasing Contract (Equipment Type - Leaseback)" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-001). The contract stipulated that for the purpose of achieving financial leasing, the lessor agreed to acquire the leased equipment owned by the lessees and then lease the leased equipment back to the lessees for their use under a financial leasing arrangement. "Leased equipment" refers to the equipment and its ancillary facilities, as well as intangible assets attached thereto, acquired by the lessor from the lessees and leased to the lessees for use, including any replacement leased equipment under the contract. Under this contract, the lessees sold their own equipment to the lessor, the lessor paid the purchase price to the lessees, and the lessees simultaneously leased back the equipment from the lessor and paid rent and other amounts due to the lessor. The lessees assumed all responsibility and risk for the selected leased assets. On the date the lessor paid the transfer price to the lessees, the lessees completed delivery of the leased equipment to the lessor by constructive possession, and ownership of the leased equipment transferred from the lessees to the lessor, which also constituted fulfillment by the lessor of its delivery obligation of the leased assets under the financial leasing contract. The purchase price of the leased equipment was RMB 200,000,000, the total rent was RMB 227,431,250, and the lease term was 60 months, with rent payable every 3 months for a total of 20 installments. The rent commencement date was the 15th day of the first calendar month following the date Zhongmin Company fully paid the principal amount of the financial lease. The lease term ran from July 15, 2016 to April 15, 2021. A deposit of RMB 10,000,000 was provided. If the lessees failed to pay rent, pre-lease interest, or other amounts due as agreed, the lessor had the right, without the lessees' consent, to deduct the corresponding unpaid amounts from the deposit paid by the lessees in the order of fees, other amounts due, penalty, damages, pre-lease interest due, and rent due. The leasing interest rate was 5.225%, which was 10% above the benchmark 1-5 year lending rate of the People's Bank of China (4.75%) at the same time. If the People's Bank of China adjusted the benchmark lending rate, the lessor could adjust the leasing interest rate in the same direction and by the same margin. The period from the date the lessor partially or fully paid the principal amount of the financial lease to the rent commencement date was the pre-lease period. During the pre-lease period, the lessees were required to pay pre-lease interest to the lessor in accordance with the "Lease Schedule," calculated on the basis of the actual principal amount of the financial lease paid by the lessor, the leasing interest rate specified in the "Lease Schedule," and the duration of the pre-lease period. At the end of the lease term, ownership of the leased assets automatically reverted to the lessees. If the lessees failed to pay the full amount of rent or other amounts due on time as stipulated in the contract, the lessees were liable to pay penalty to the lessor on the overdue amount at a rate of 0.05% per day until full payment was made. If any installment of rent or other amounts due was not paid by the lessees as stipulated in this contract, the lessor had the right to require the lessees to assume liability for breach of contract as stipulated in this contract or to compensate the lessor for all losses incurred thereby. The lessor had the right to declare all or part of the lessees' debts under this contract due immediately and demand that the lessees immediately pay all penalty, damages, all or part of the overdue rent and future rent, with penalty calculated as overdue amount x 0.05% x number of days overdue (from the day after the payment deadline set by the lessor's notice to the actual payment date), and damages calculated at 1% of the principal portion of all future rent. Appendix 1, the List of Leased Equipment, showed that the leased assets under this contract were the equipment and facilities corresponding to the following gas stations (Table 1), with specific lists contained in Table 2 and Table 3. The gas stations in Table 1 were Xingfu Road Station, Zhuyeshan Station, and Changqing Station, with a total assessed value of RMB 274,783,700. Table 2 was a detailed list of fixed assets - machinery and equipment, comprising 144 items. Table 3 was a detailed list of fixed assets - structures and other auxiliary facilities, comprising 51 items.

On the same day, Party A Zhongmin Company and Party B Qingdao Zhongtian Company entered into a "Consulting Service Contract" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-ZX), stipulating that Party B entrusted Party A to provide economic consulting services regarding Party B's management and operations as agreed. The contract specified the content and method of services. After Party A completed the relevant economic consulting services, Party B was to issue a confirmation letter to Party A, and Party B was to make payment in accordance with Party A's payment notice. The consulting service fee was RMB 13,500,000. On the same day, Qingdao Zhongtian Company issued a confirmation letter confirming that Zhongmin Company had provided consulting opinions on the economic consulting matters of Qingdao Zhongtian Company in accordance with the contract, and Qingdao Zhongtian Company would pay a service fee of RMB 13,500,000. Zhongmin Company stated that this consulting service fee was for the three financial leasing contracts (hereinafter referred to as the three main contracts) numbered CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-001, CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-002, and CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-003, with each being RMB 4,500,000.

On June 22, 2016, the guarantors Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo and the creditor Zhongmin Company entered into a "Natural Person Guarantee Contract" (Contract No. CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-ZRR). The contract stipulated that the creditor, as lessor, had entered into the three main contracts with the guaranteed persons, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company. To ensure the performance of the three main contracts, and at the request of the lessees, the guarantors agreed to provide an irrevocable joint and several liability guarantee for all debts owed by the lessees to the creditor under the three main contracts. The guaranteed principal debt was all claims of the creditor against the lessees under the three main contracts. The scope of the guarantee covered all pre-lease interest, all rent, penalty, compensation, damages, and various expenses incurred by the creditor to realize its claims (including but not limited to litigation fees, arbitration fees, lawyer fees, travel expenses, property preservation fees, enforcement fees, service fees, notarization fees, and auction and appraisal fees for taking back leased assets under the main contracts), and all other amounts payable by the lessees under the three main contracts. The guarantee period ran from the date of execution of this contract until two years after the expiry of the term for the lessees to perform all debts under the three main contracts. Regardless of whether the creditor had entered into guarantee contracts with any other guarantor under the three main contracts in any form of security, the guarantor voluntarily agreed to assume guarantee liability under this contract, and promised that under any other form of security, regardless of any circumstances that might affect the creditor's priority right to satisfaction, the guarantor would not claim exemption from guarantee liability to the extent that the creditor's priority right to satisfaction was prejudiced.

On June 22, 2016, the pledgor, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and the pledgee, Zhongmin Company, entered into a Pledge Contract with contract number CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-ZY. The contract stipulated that, to ensure the realization of the rights of the pledgee as the lessor under the three main contracts signed with the lessees, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company, the pledgor and the pledgee agreed, through consultation, to use the gas operation license approved by the Wuhan Urban Management Committee for the pledgor as security for the realization of the pledgee's rights under the three main contracts. The principal claim secured by the pledge was all claims of the pledgee against the lessees under the three main contracts. The scope of the pledge covered all debts that the lessees should perform to the pledgee under the three main contracts, including but not limited to all rents, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and various expenses paid by the creditor for realizing its claims (including but not limited to litigation fees, arbitration fees, lawyer fees, travel expenses, and auction and appraisal fees for recovering the leased property under the main contracts), and all other amounts payable by the lessees. The pledge registration period was five years. If the pledgee's rights under the three main contracts were not fully realized upon expiration, the pledgee had the right to apply for an extension, and the pledgor should cooperate. The pledged gas operation license was Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., License No. E20150100000IJ; the gas station supply licenses were: Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Baofeng Road Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 013-16; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Changfeng Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 017-16; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Changqing Road Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 033-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Jintan Road Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 008-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Junshan Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 007-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Shilipu Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 034-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Xingfu Road Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 001-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Xiongchu Avenue Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 014-16; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Yejin Avenue Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 019-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Yuejiazui Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 009-15; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Zhuyeshan CNG Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 017-14; Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd., Zoujiawan Natural Gas Filling Station, Supply License No. RG (Vehicle) 018-15. On June 25, 2016, the above pledged property was registered as a unified registration of chattel property rights - initial registration at the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China, with registration certificate number XXX97.

On June 22, 2016, the mortgagor, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and the mortgagee, Zhongmin Company, entered into a Mortgage Contract with contract number CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-DY. The contract stipulated that the lessees, Wuhan Zhongneng Company and Qingdao Zhongtian Company, had signed the three main contracts and their appendices with the mortgagee. To ensure the performance of the three main contracts, the mortgagor agreed to create a mortgage on the property it had the right to dispose of to provide mortgage guarantee for all claims of the mortgagee against the lessees under the three main contracts. The principal claim secured by the mortgage was all claims of the mortgagee against the lessees under the three main contracts. The period of the mortgage guarantee was from the effective date of the contract until all debts of the lessees under the three main contracts were fully performed. The scope of the mortgage guarantee covered all debts that the lessees should perform to the mortgagee under the three main contracts, including but not limited to all rents, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and various expenses paid by the creditor for realizing its claims (including but not limited to litigation fees, arbitration fees, lawyer fees, travel expenses, and auction and appraisal fees for recovering the leased property under the main contracts), and all other amounts payable by the lessees. The mortgaged property consisted of land and buildings of the filling stations. The list of mortgaged property in Appendix 1 to the contract showed: 1. Land parcel XX in the Wuhan Economic and Technological Development Zone, with an area of 10,189.15 square meters, land certificate number Wu Kai Guo Yong (2012) No. 29, owned by Wuhan Zhongneng Company; 2. Land parcel at XX Road, Hanyang District, with an area of 6,540.22 square meters, land certificate number Wu Guo Yong (2010) No. 205, owned by Wuhan Zhongneng Company. Both parties acknowledged that no mortgage registration was carried out on the mortgaged property.

On June 22, 2016, the lessor, Zhongmin Company, the lessees, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and the repurchaser, Changchun Zhongtian Company, entered into a Repurchase Agreement with contract number CMIFL-2016-053-SB-HZ-HG. The contract stipulated that, whereas the lessor, Zhongmin Company, and the lessees, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company, had signed the three main contracts, the lessor, lessees, and repurchaser reached an agreement on the repurchase of the leased property under the three main contracts. The subject matter of repurchase was: 1. The leased equipment under the three main contracts; 2. The lease claims of the lessor against the lessees under the three main contracts (lease claims under this agreement refer to the lessor's right to collect unpaid rents and other amounts payable from the lessees, as well as other contractual rights). When the lessees committed a default event of overdue rent for three working days in the current period or a cumulative total of ten working days, the lessor had the right to require the repurchaser to perform the repurchase obligation. When the repurchase conditions under the agreement were fulfilled, if the lessor required the repurchaser to perform the repurchase obligation, it should issue a Repurchase Notice. The Repurchase Notice should specify the reason for repurchase, the repurchase price and basis for calculation, the payment period, etc. If the repurchase conditions were fulfilled and the repurchaser failed to perform the repurchase obligation as agreed, paying the repurchase price in full and on time, the repurchaser was deemed to be in breach. The repurchaser should not only continue to fully perform the repurchase obligation but also pay liquidated damages to the lessor at a daily rate of 0.05% of the overdue unpaid amount. The agreement was valid from its effective date until the full realization of the lessor's lease claims under the three main contracts. Zhongmin Company did not issue a Repurchase Notice to Changchun Zhongtian Company but indicated at the trial that it had issued a notice to Changchun Zhongtian Company through litigation.

On June 22, 2016, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company issued an acceptance letter for the leased equipment to Zhongmin Company. On June 24, 2016, Zhongmin Company paid RMB 480,000,000 to Qingdao Zhongtian Company. On June 27, 2016, Zhongmin Company paid RMB 120,000,000 to Qingdao Zhongtian Company. On June 27, 2016, the leased property in this case was registered as a unified registration of chattel property rights - initial registration at the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China, with registration certificate number XXX99.

On June 24, 2016, Qingdao Zhongtian Company paid RMB 43,500,000 to Zhongmin Company. Zhongmin Company acknowledged that this amount represented the security deposits of RMB 10,000,000 each and service fees of RMB 4,500,000 each for the three main contracts.

Qingdao Zhongtian Company made payments to Zhongmin Company as follows: On July 15, 2016, RMB 39,613,999.99, which Zhongmin Company stated included the first period rents of the three main contracts (RMB 12,612,500 each) and the pre-lease interest as agreed in the contracts (RMB 1,776,499.99); on October 14, 2016, RMB 37,445,625; on January 13, 2017, RMB 37,053,750; on April 14, 2017, RMB 36,661,875; on July 14, 2017, RMB 36,270,000; on October 13, 2017, RMB 35,878,125; on January 15, 2018, RMB 35,486,250; on April 13, 2018, RMB 35,094,375. Zhongmin Company stated that the above amounts were all payments of rents for the three main contracts together, and the rents for the three main contracts were identical. On July 13, 2018, Qingdao Zhongtian Company paid RMB 4,702,500 to Zhongmin Company. On August 6, 2018, Qingdao Zhongtian Company paid RMB 5,000,000 to Zhongmin Company. Zhongmin Company claimed that these two payments were for partial payment of the ninth period rents of the three main contracts, with corresponding amounts of RMB 6,567,500, RMB 1,567,500, and RMB 1,567,500, and the corresponding arrears were RMB 5,000,000, RMB 10,000,000, and RMB 10,000,000. Regarding the issue of Zhongmin Company's notice of accelerated maturity, Zhongmin Company stated that it had previously made oral collection notices but asserted accelerated maturity through litigation. As of the first inquiry hearing of the court of first instance on October 22, 2019, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company owed Zhongmin Company: RMB 5,000,000 for the ninth period rent due on July 15, 2018; RMB 11,436,875 for the tenth period rent due on October 15, 2018; RMB 11,306,250 for the eleventh period rent due on January 15, 2019; RMB 11,175,625 for the twelfth period rent due on April 15, 2019; RMB 11,045,000 for the thirteenth period rent due on July 15, 2019; and RMB 10,914,375 for the fourteenth period rent due on October 15, 2019. The remaining unmatured rents were from the fifteenth to the twentieth periods, totaling RMB 62,743,125.

The court of first instance held that the following issues were in dispute in this case: 1. The nature and validity of the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback); 2. Whether Zhongmin Company's claims for overdue rents, unmatured rents, and corresponding liquidated damages for overdue payment could be upheld; 3. Whether Zhongmin Company's claims for damages and lawyer fees could be upheld; 4. Whether Zhongmin Company's claims for security rights could be upheld; 5. Whether Zhongmin Company's claim for repurchase liability could be upheld.

1. Nature and validity of the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) in question.

A finance lease contract is a contract under which the lessor, based on the lessee's choice of seller and leased property, purchases the leased property from the seller, provides it to the lessee for use, and the lessee pays rent. The People's Court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 237 of the Contract Law of the PRC, combined with the nature, value, composition of rent, and the rights and obligations of the parties under the contract, determine whether a finance lease legal relationship is constituted. The Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) signed by Zhongmin Company, Qingdao Zhongtian Company, and Wuhan Zhongneng Company represented the true intention of the parties, and its content did not violate laws or regulations. Regarding the leased property: although the lists of leased property in Appendices 2 and 3 of the three Finance Lease Contracts (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) were identical, Table 1 clearly identified different filling stations and specified the equipment and facilities corresponding to Table 1, with the specific list contained in Tables 2 and 3. Therefore, the leased property could be specified. Regarding the value of the leased property: it had been determined by an appraisal institution, and there was no contrary evidence to negate the value of the leased property. Therefore, the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) in question had the characteristics of providing financing and leasing assets. It should be determined that a finance lease contract relationship existed among Zhongmin Company, Qingdao Zhongtian Company, and Wuhan Zhongneng Company. The defenses of Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Changchun Zhongtian Company that the contracts in question were corporate loan contracts and invalid lacked corresponding factual basis and were not adopted.

2. Regarding Zhongmin Company's claims for overdue rents, unmatured rents, and corresponding liquidated damages for overdue payment.

Zhongmin Company had performed its payment obligations under the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback), completed the acquisition of the equipment, and leased the equipment to Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company for continued use. Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company should pay rent on time in accordance with the contract. Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company failed to pay rent on time, which constituted a breach of contract under the terms of the contract. Zhongmin Company was entitled, in accordance with the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback), to require Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company to pay overdue unpaid rents, all unmatured rents, and liquidated damages for overdue payment. Therefore, Zhongmin Company's corresponding claims were upheld. Zhongmin Company asserted accelerated maturity through litigation. Taking into account a reasonable performance period, the date of the first inquiry hearing of the court of first instance, October 22, 2019, was determined as the date of accelerated maturity of the rents.

Regarding the offset of the security deposit: Qingdao Zhongtian Company claimed that the security deposit was RMB 14,500,000. Upon examination, the contract stipulated that the security deposit was RMB 10,000,000. Zhongmin Company provided a Consulting Services Contract separately signed with Qingdao Zhongtian Company and corresponding evidence, proving that the service fees were RMB 4,500,000. Therefore, the security deposit was RMB 10,000,000. The contract stipulated the order of offset of the security deposit, which should be applied to fees, other amounts payable, liquidated damages, damages for losses, pre-lease interest payable, and rents payable, in that order.

3. Regarding Zhongmin Company's claims for damages and lawyer fees.

If one party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach of contract, such as continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses. The parties may agree that, in the event of a breach, the breaching party shall pay a certain amount of liquidated damages to the other party based on the breach, and may also agree on the method for calculating the amount of compensation for losses arising from the breach. The Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) in question stipulated liquidated damages and damages for losses. Damages for losses also constitute losses arising from breach. Zhongmin Company had already claimed liquidated damages and could not prove that the liquidated damages were insufficient to cover its losses. Therefore, its claim for damages for losses was not upheld. Regarding lawyer fees, Zhongmin Company did not provide corresponding evidence to prove the actual incurrence of such fees, and thus the claim was not upheld. The defense of Qingdao Zhongtian Company on this point was adopted.

4. Regarding Zhongmin Company's claims for security rights.

Regarding the guarantee liability of Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo: the Personal Guarantee Contracts signed by Zhongmin Company with Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo represented the true intention of the parties, and their content did not violate laws or regulations. They were legal and valid. Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo should bear joint and several guarantee liability for the debts of Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company arising from the Finance Lease Contract (Equipment Type - Sale and Leaseback) in question. After assuming the guarantee liability, Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo had the right to seek recourse from Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company. Regarding the pledge rights claimed by Zhongmin Company: the Pledge Contract signed by Zhongmin Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company was legal and valid, and registration was carried out, so the pledge right was effectively established. Zhongmin Company's claim to be entitled to priority in satisfaction from the gas operation right under the Pledge Contract had a factual basis and was upheld.

Regarding the mortgage rights claimed by Zhongmin Company: the Mortgage Contract signed by Zhongmin Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company represented the true intention of the parties and was legal and valid. However, after signing the mortgage contract, the parties did not carry out mortgage registration. Therefore, the mortgage right was not established. Zhongmin Company's claim to be entitled to priority in satisfaction from the mortgage lacked corresponding factual basis and was not upheld. Regarding the liability for damages arising from the failure to establish the mortgage right: since Wuhan Zhongneng Company itself had an obligation to pay, even if such liability for damages arose, it would be covered by the payment obligation. Therefore, Zhongmin Company's claim for mortgage rights was not upheld.

5. Regarding Zhongmin Company's claim for repurchase liability.

The Repurchase Agreement signed by Zhongmin Company, Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and Changchun Zhongtian Company represented the true intention of the parties, and its content did not violate laws or regulations. It was legal and valid. Each party should perform its respective obligations in accordance with the agreement. Zhongmin Company's claim that Changchun Zhongtian Company should perform the repurchase liability for the lease claims of Zhongmin Company against Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company under the Finance Lease Contract was consistent with the contract terms and was upheld. Changchun Zhongtian Company's defense that the contract was invalid and that it should not bear liability, but failed to provide evidence to support its claims, was not upheld.

The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 6, Article 8, Article 237, and Article 248 of the Contract Law of the PRC; Article 18, Article 21(1), Article 31, and Article 75 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC; Article 180 and Article 187 of the Property Law of the PRC; Article 1, Article 2, and Article 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Finance Lease Contracts; and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled as follows: 1. Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, pay Zhongmin Company the overdue unpaid rents of RMB 60,878,125 and the accelerated maturity rents of RMB 62,743,125, totaling RMB 123,621,250; 2. Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, pay Zhongmin Company liquidated damages for overdue payment (calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% on the overdue amounts for the ninth to fourteenth period rents from the respective due dates until October 22, 2019; and calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% on the amount of RMB 123,621,250 from October 23, 2019, until the date of actual payment); the security deposit of RMB 10,000,000 shall be first applied to offset the liquidated damages for overdue payment, and any remaining amount shall be applied to offset the payment obligation under item 1 above; 3. Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo shall bear joint and several payment liability for the payment obligations under items 1 and 2 above; after assuming the guarantee liability, Deng Tianzhou and Huang Bo shall have the right to seek recourse from Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company; 4. For the payment obligations under items 1 and 2 above, Zhongmin Company shall have the right to be entitled to priority in satisfaction from the pledge property of Wuhan Zhongneng Company under the Pledge Contract within the scope of the pledge guarantee; 5. Changchun Zhongtian Company shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, pay the repurchase price to Zhongmin Company in accordance with the payment obligations under items 1 and 2 above; after Changchun Zhongtian Company pays the repurchase price, the corresponding lease claims shall be transferred to Changchun Zhongtian Company; 6. If any one of Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, Deng Tianzhou, Huang Bo, or Changchun Zhongtian Company performs the above payment obligations, the corresponding payment obligations of the other parties to Zhongmin Company shall be discharged; 7. Zhongmin Company's other claims were dismissed.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 683,084 and the preservation fee of RMB 5,000 were to be borne by Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, Deng Tianzhou, Huang Bo, and Changchun Zhongtian Company.

Wuhan Zhongneng Company, dissatisfied with the above judgment, appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court, requesting that the original judgment be set aside and the claim by Zhongmin Company for payment of overdue rents and liquidated damages by Wuhan Zhongneng Company and for the right to priority in satisfaction from the pledge property of Wuhan Zhongneng Company be dismissed.

Changchun Zhongtian Co., Ltd. appealed against the above judgment to the Tianjin High People's Court, requesting that the original judgment be reversed and the claim for Changchun Zhongtian to assume the repurchase obligation be dismissed.

During the second instance, Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. and Changchun Zhongtian Co., Ltd. additionally submitted a description of equity relations, an announcement of Changchun Zhongtian's reply on the new violations of guarantee matters, the articles of association of Changchun Zhongtian as revised in November 2015, a resolution announcement of Changchun Zhongtian, an audit report, an explanation of the board resolution of Changchun Zhongtian, a list of board members of Changchun Zhongtian in 2016, a board resolution of Changchun Zhongtian in 2016, the external guarantee system of Changchun Zhongtian, an explanation of fund flows, and a disciplinary decision. Zhongmin Co., Ltd. additionally submitted a board resolution of Changchun Zhongtian dated June 22, 2016. The court of second instance organized the parties to exchange evidence and conduct cross-examination. For evidence to which the parties did not object as to authenticity, the court of second instance confirmed it and placed it on file as supporting evidence. For the disputed evidence, the court determined as follows: The announcement of Changchun Zhongtian's reply on the new violations of guarantee matters was a document on a public information website; the external guarantee system of Changchun Zhongtian was a publicly disclosed document; the court confirmed the authenticity of the above evidence. Zhongmin Co., Ltd. submitted the original of the board resolution, and the court confirmed the authenticity of this evidence.

The court of second instance, upon trial, found that the facts found by the court of first instance were supported by relevant evidence, and the court confirmed them. It was additionally found that: At the time of signing the Repurchase Agreement, Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. was a shareholder of Changchun Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. was a wholly-owned sub-subsidiary of Changchun Zhongtian Co., Ltd. Article 42 of the articles of association of Changchun Zhongtian as revised in November 2015 provided: "The following external guarantee acts of the company must be submitted to the general meeting of shareholders for deliberation and approval: (4) Guarantees where the single guarantee amount exceeds 10% of the latest audited net assets; (5) Guarantees provided to shareholders, actual controllers, and their affiliated parties." Article 104 provided: "With the authorization of the general meeting of shareholders, the board of directors of the company has the authority to approve external guarantees that are not subject to the approval of the general meeting of shareholders. External guarantees that require approval by the board of directors must be deliberated and approved by more than two-thirds of all directors and a resolution must be passed. Violations of the authority of the general meeting of shareholders or the board of directors to approve external guarantees as specified in the articles of association shall result in the corresponding legal liability and economic liability of the responsible person." On March 18, 2016, Changchun Zhongtian held an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and passed the "Proposal on Requesting the General Meeting of Shareholders to Authorize the Board of Directors with the Authority to Approve External Guarantees." To meet the financing and operational needs of the company and its subsidiaries and to improve management efficiency, for guarantees provided by the company to its subsidiaries, by subsidiaries to the company, or between subsidiaries, if the total guarantee amount did not exceed RMB 2.2 billion, the general meeting of shareholders authorized the board of directors to deliberate on the guarantee matters when they arose. The board resolution submitted by Zhongmin Co., Ltd. recorded that Changchun Zhongtian held a board meeting on June 22, 2016, at Chaoyang District, Beijing; all directors were notified in accordance with the law before the meeting, and those attending were members of the new board of directors elected by the shareholders' meeting. The resolution passed at the meeting was that Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., as joint lessees, would conduct financial leasing business with Zhongmin Co., Ltd. and signed three financial leasing contracts, each for RMB 200 million, totaling RMB 600 million. To ensure the smooth progress of this business, Changchun Zhongtian was approved to sign the Repurchase Agreement to provide repurchase for each financial leasing transaction.

The court of second instance held that this case involved a dispute over a financial leasing contract. In light of the appeals and defense opinions of the parties, the focal issues in dispute were: 1. The nature and validity of the Financial Leasing Contract and the Pledge Contract involved in the case; 2. The nature and validity of the Repurchase Agreement involved in the case, and whether Changchun Zhongtian should assume the repurchase obligation.

1. Regarding the nature and validity of the Financial Leasing Contract and the Pledge Contract involved in the case.

First, on June 22, 2016, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. signed the Financial Leasing Contract. The parties had no objection to the authenticity of the signatures and seals on the contract. The contract represented the true intention of each party, and its contents did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Thus, the validity of the contract was confirmed. According to the contract, Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., as lessees, sold equipment owned by them to Zhongmin Co., Ltd., which then leased it back to the lessees for use. Therefore, the nature of the Financial Leasing Contract in this case was a sale-and-leaseback arrangement. The leased property in the case consisted of the equipment and facilities of three gas stations owned by Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. Zhongmin Co., Ltd. provided an appraisal report for those gas stations, and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. also confirmed that the leased property existed. Zhongmin Co., Ltd., Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. formed a financial leasing legal relationship, and each party should perform its respective obligations in accordance with the Financial Leasing Contract.

Second, the Financial Leasing Contract in the case stipulated that the lessor, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., upon meeting the corresponding conditions, would pay the transfer price in a lump sum to one of the lessees, Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. On the date of such payment, the lessees would complete delivery to the lessor by constructive delivery. The lessor would be the sole owner of the leased equipment, and the lessees should pay rent to the lessor during the lease term. After the contract was signed, Zhongmin Co., Ltd. paid the transfer price to Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. issued a receipt for the leased equipment to Zhongmin Co., Ltd., and Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. also paid part of the rent. These facts demonstrated that all parties had actually performed the Financial Leasing Contract. Although Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. claimed that it did not receive the transfer price or pay rent, given that it agreed in the Financial Leasing Contract that the transfer price would be paid to Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and the fact that Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. paid rent did not exempt Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. from its contractual obligations as a lessee. Therefore, Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd.'s claim that it did not actually perform the Financial Leasing Contract and its request to confirm the contract as invalid lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported.

Finally, regarding Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd.'s claim that the Pledge Contract was invalid due to lack of true expression of intention, at the time of signing the Financial Leasing Contract, Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. and Zhongmin Co., Ltd. signed the Pledge Contract, agreeing that Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. would pledge its property to guarantee the performance of the Financial Leasing Contract. Since the contract was confirmed by the signature and seal of Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., and the Pledge Contract had also undergone public registration procedures, there were no circumstances rendering the contract invalid. Although Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. argued that the contract did not represent its true intention, it did not provide sufficient evidence to prove this, and its claim was not supported.

2. Regarding the nature and validity of the Repurchase Agreement involved in the case, and whether Changchun Zhongtian should assume the repurchase obligation.

On June 22, 2016, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., and Changchun Zhongtian Co., Ltd. signed the Repurchase Agreement, stipulating that whereas Zhongmin Co., Ltd. had signed the Financial Leasing Contract with Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., in the event of a default event such as the lessees' overdue rent payment, Zhongmin Co., Ltd. had the right to require Changchun Zhongtian to perform the repurchase obligation. The subject of the repurchase was the leased equipment and the lease receivables under the Financial Leasing Contract. The parties disputed the nature and validity of the Repurchase Agreement. The court of second instance analyzed this as follows:

(1) Regarding the determination of the nature of the Repurchase Agreement.

First, Article 14 of the Financial Leasing Contract in the case stipulated that to ensure the lessees performed their rent payment obligations and other obligations under the contract, the lessees should provide the lessor with guarantees that met the lessor's requirements and bear the relevant costs themselves. The guarantees required by the lessor under the contract included the Repurchase Agreement. Although Changchun Zhongtian was not a signatory to the Financial Leasing Contract, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., as the lessor under the Financial Leasing Contract, should have known and acknowledged that the Repurchase Agreement had a guarantee function. Second, to determine the nature of the Repurchase Agreement, one should start from the content of the parties' expressions of intention. If the parties had an expression of intention for a guarantee, it should be determined that a guarantee legal relationship existed. In this case, the prerequisite for signing the Repurchase Agreement was that the parties had already signed the Financial Leasing Contract. The condition for Changchun Zhongtian, as the repurchaser, to assume the repurchase liability was the occurrence of a default event under the Financial Leasing Contract. Therefore, from the perspective of the content of the debt assumed by Changchun Zhongtian and the order of obligation performance by the parties, it could be determined that a guarantee contract relationship existed between Zhongmin Co., Ltd. and Changchun Zhongtian under the Repurchase Agreement. Finally, although the Repurchase Agreement was a contract with a guarantee function, it did not belong to the types of security interests established under the Property Law of the PRC and differed from the unilateral and gratuitous nature of traditional guarantee methods. Therefore, the court of second instance determined that the nature of the Repurchase Agreement was an atypical guarantee, and in determining its validity, it should be distinguished from traditional guarantee types.

(2) Regarding the validity of the Repurchase Agreement.

Since the Repurchase Agreement was a contract with a guarantee function, according to Article 16 of the Company Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law), when a company makes investments in other enterprises or provides guarantees to others, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association, be resolved by the board of directors or the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. If the articles of association impose limits on the total amount of investment or guarantees and the amount of individual investments or guarantees, the limits shall not be exceeded. If a company provides a guarantee to its shareholders or actual controllers, it must be passed by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. The shareholders referred to in the preceding paragraph or shareholders controlled by the actual controller referred to in the preceding paragraph shall not participate in the vote on the matters specified in the preceding paragraph. Such vote shall be passed by more than half of the voting rights held by other shareholders attending the meeting. Therefore, the validity of the Repurchase Agreement under which Changchun Zhongtian provided guarantees for Qingdao Zhongtian and Wuhan Zhongneng should be determined in accordance with the above legal provisions.

Qingdao Zhongtian was a shareholder of Changchun Zhongtian. According to the Company Law, the guarantee matter should be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders of Changchun Zhongtian. In this case, Zhongmin Co., Ltd. did not provide the above resolution documents. Therefore, this case should focus on examining the validity of the guarantee provided by Changchun Zhongtian for Wuhan Zhongneng. In this regard, the court of second instance held that because Changchun Zhongtian was a listed company, according to legal and regulatory requirements, listed companies should publicly disclose major matters. If Zhongmin Co., Ltd., as a creditor, entered into a guarantee contract based on information publicly disclosed by the listed company regarding the guarantee matter having been approved by a resolution of the corporate body, the people's court should confirm it as valid. However, when a listed company has not publicly disclosed a contract of a guarantee nature, the contract is not necessarily invalid. Instead, when examining the validity of the contract, the creditor should be subject to a substantive review obligation to determine whether the signing of the guarantee nature contract represented the true intention of the listed company, whether it had been reviewed by a resolution-making body in accordance with the company's articles of association and without violating legal provisions, whether the formation of the corporate body's resolution was lawful, and whether it had a material impact on the public nature of the listed company. In this regard, the court of second instance analyzed as follows:

1. Wuhan Zhongneng was a wholly-owned sub-subsidiary of Changchun Zhongtian. According to Article 16 of the Company Law, this guarantee matter fell under a guarantee provided by the company to a person other than a shareholder or actual controller. In such a case, the resolution-making body should be strictly examined in accordance with the company's articles of association. According to the articles of association of Changchun Zhongtian as revised in November 2015, the resolution-making bodies for external guarantee matters were the general meeting of shareholders and the board of directors. The articles of association made specific provisions regarding the different guarantee matters subject to the above resolution bodies, and provided that the board of directors exercised other powers authorized by the general meeting of shareholders. In the resolution passed by the general meeting of shareholders of Changchun Zhongtian on March 18, 2016, it was explicitly stipulated that guarantees for subsidiaries, where the total amount did not exceed RMB 2.2 billion, were authorized to the board of directors for deliberation and approval. Combined with the board resolution and the authorization proposal of Changchun Zhongtian, the resolution-making body for the guarantee provided to Wuhan Zhongneng in this case should be the board of directors of Changchun Zhongtian.

2. During the second instance, Zhongmin Co., Ltd. submitted the board resolution of Changchun Zhongtian dated June 22, 2016, which detailed the time, place, pre-meeting notification procedures, and content of the vote at the board meeting. The board resolution was signed and confirmed by six board members and also bore the corporate seal of Changchun Zhongtian. Changchun Zhongtian had no objection to the authenticity of the corporate seal on the board resolution but claimed that the signatures of the board members were forged, that the board resolution was not filed with the company, and that the board was convened irregularly. In this regard, the court of second instance held: From a formal perspective, since the guarantee for Wuhan Zhongneng fell within the approval authority of the board of directors, the board resolution submitted by Zhongmin Co., Ltd. bore the seal of Changchun Zhongtian, which preliminarily proved that Zhongmin Co., Ltd. had reviewed the board resolution. From a substantive perspective, the signatories on the board resolution were all directors of Changchun Zhongtian, and the number of signing directors was six, meeting the requirement in the articles of association that approval by more than two-thirds of the directors must be obtained. Changchun Zhongtian claimed that some of the signatures on the resolution were forged, but it only provided a written explanation and WeChat chat records with the directors. It did not apply for judicial authentication of the authenticity of the signatures, and the relevant persons mentioned in the explanation did not appear in court to be questioned. Therefore, its claim was not accepted. Furthermore, the board resolution clearly recorded the time and place of the meeting and stated that the pre-meeting notification procedures had been completed. Combined with the signatures of the board members and the affixing of the company seal, it could be proven that on June 22, 2016, Changchun Zhongtian held a board meeting and passed the matter of providing a repurchase for Wuhan Zhongneng. Although Changchun Zhongtian claimed that the board resolution was not filed with the company, this claim could not negate the fact that the meeting was held. Therefore, even though the repurchase matter was not publicly announced, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., based on the board resolution of Changchun Zhongtian, signed the Repurchase Agreement with Changchun Zhongtian and had fulfilled the duty of good faith review. The nature of this agreement should be valid.

3. Although Changchun Zhongtian was a listed company and its nature involved the public interest, and generally speaking, a company's external guarantee matters affect the interests of its shareholders and the healthy development of the securities market, the guarantee matter in this case was not a typical guarantee such as a suretyship, mortgage, or pledge. According to the Repurchase Agreement, after performing the repurchase obligation, Changchun Zhongtian had the right to obtain the leased property under the Financial Leasing Contract, and Zhongmin Co., Ltd. also agreed to this. Given that the leased property in the case actually existed and had been appraised by an appraisal institution, after Changchun Zhongtian performed the repurchase obligation, it could obtain ownership of the leased property to protect its own legitimate rights and interests. Therefore, because this type of guarantee differed from traditional typical guarantees, Changchun Zhongtian could obtain the corresponding leased property after performing the Repurchase Agreement, thereby reducing the risk after assuming the guarantee liability. In the circumstances where Zhongmin Co., Ltd. had provided evidence that the matter had been approved by a resolution of the corporate body, and Wuhan Zhongneng should assume the liability of the lessee, the original court's judgment ordering Changchun Zhongtian to assume the repurchase liability was not improper.

In summary, the court of second instance held that the facts found in the first instance judgment were clear and the judgment was correct. The appeal requests of Wuhan Zhongneng and Changchun Zhongtian could not be sustained. The court issued a civil judgment (2020) Jin Min Zhong No. 370 on July 27, 2020, and, in accordance with Item 1 of the first paragraph of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, ordered that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,366,168 was to be borne by Wuhan Zhongneng in the amount of RMB 683,084 and by Changchun Zhongtian in the amount of RMB 683,084.

During the retrial, no party submitted new evidence. The parties had no objection to the facts found in the first and second instance judgments, and this Court confirmed them upon trial. This Court additionally found that Changchun Zhongtian completed the industrial and commercial registration change procedures to change its company name to Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. on October 14, 2020, and obtained a new Business License from the relevant registration authority.

This Court, upon retrial, held that there were two focal issues in this case: First, whether Wuhan Zhongneng should bear liability; second, whether Changchun Zhongtian should bear liability.

1. Regarding whether Wuhan Zhongneng should bear liability.

First, on June 22, 2016, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. signed the Financial Leasing Contract. The parties had no objection to the authenticity of the signatures and seals on the contract. The contract represented the true intention of each party, and its contents did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; the contract was valid. According to the contract, Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd., as lessees, sold equipment owned by them to Zhongmin Co., Ltd., which then leased it back to the lessees for use. The leased property in the case consisted of the equipment and facilities of three gas stations owned by Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. Zhongmin Co., Ltd. provided an appraisal report for those gas stations, and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. also confirmed that the leased property existed. Zhongmin Co., Ltd., Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. formed a financial leasing legal relationship, and each party should perform its respective obligations in accordance with the Financial Leasing Contract. Although Wuhan Zhongneng claimed that it did not follow the procedural rules stipulated in its articles of association when signing the Financial Leasing Contract, thereby rendering the contract invalid, the restrictions on the legal representative's authority in the company's articles of association cannot be used to oppose a bona fide third party. Zhongmin Co., Ltd. was not obliged to pay attention to the internal procedural rules of Wuhan Zhongneng. Therefore, the above claim of Wuhan Zhongneng lacked factual and legal basis, and this Court did not support it.

Second, the Financial Leasing Contract in the case stipulated that the lessor, Zhongmin Co., Ltd., upon meeting the corresponding conditions, would pay the transfer price in a lump sum to one of the lessees, Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. On the date of such payment, the lessees would complete delivery to the lessor by constructive delivery. The lessor would be the sole owner of the leased equipment, and the lessees should pay rent to the lessor during the lease term. After the contract was signed, Zhongmin Co., Ltd. paid the transfer price to Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. issued a receipt for the leased equipment to Zhongmin Co., Ltd., and Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. also paid part of the rent. That is, all parties had actually performed the Financial Leasing Contract. Although Wuhan Zhongneng claimed that it did not receive the transfer price or pay rent, it agreed in the Financial Leasing Contract that the transfer price would be paid in a lump sum to Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd., and the fact that Qingdao Zhongtian Co., Ltd. paid rent did not exempt Wuhan Zhongneng Co., Ltd. from its contractual obligations as a lessee. Therefore, Wuhan Zhongneng's claim that it was not a party to the financial leasing contract on the ground that it did not actually perform the Financial Leasing Contract lacked factual and legal basis, and this Court did not support it.

2. Whether Changchun Zhongtian Company should bear contractual liability

First, Zhongmin Company entered into the Repurchase Agreement with Qingdao Zhongtian Company, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, and Changchun Zhongtian Company, stipulating that when a default event occurs under the Financial Leasing Contract by Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company, Zhongmin Company has the right to require the repurchaser, Changchun Zhongtian Company, to perform the repurchase obligation. The subject matter of the repurchase comprises the leased equipment under the Financial Leasing Contract and the lease receivables held by Zhongmin Company against Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company. From the content of the obligations assumed by Changchun Zhongtian Company and the parties' agreement on the order of performance, Zhongmin Company and Changchun Zhongtian Company reached a consensus on guarantee in the Repurchase Agreement, establishing a guarantee contractual relationship, the nature of which is an atypical guarantee. Article 14 of the Financial Leasing Contract in question expressly stipulates that to ensure the lessee's payment of rent and other obligations under this contract, the lessee shall provide the lessor with a guarantee acceptable to the lessor and bear the relevant costs themselves, and the guarantee required by the lessor from the lessee includes the Repurchase Agreement in question. Therefore, as the lessor under the Financial Leasing Contract, Zhongmin Company was fully aware of and accepted the guarantee function of the Repurchase Agreement. In summary, the original judgment's determination that the Repurchase Agreement is a contract with a guarantee function and is an atypical guarantee is not erroneous. Zhongmin Company's defense that the execution of the Repurchase Agreement is not subject to the provisions on guarantees provided by a company to external parties and does not require the procedures of a board of directors' or shareholders' meeting cannot be sustained.

Second, under the Financial Leasing Contract in question, Qingdao Zhongtian Company and Wuhan Zhongneng Company bear joint and several common debts to Zhongmin Company for the payment of rent and other sums. Changchun Zhongtian Company provided a guarantee for this debt by signing the Repurchase Agreement. Qingdao Zhongtian Company is a shareholder of Changchun Zhongtian Company. Furthermore, based on the contractual stipulations and actual performance, the entire finance lease payment was made in one lump sum to Qingdao Zhongtian Company, and the rent was also actually paid by Qingdao Zhongtian Company. Therefore, in this case, Changchun Zhongtian Company essentially provided a guarantee for its shareholder, Qingdao Zhongtian Company, and must be reviewed in accordance with the procedures for a company providing a guarantee to its shareholders. The procedural requirements cannot be lowered simply because another joint and several debtor, Wuhan Zhongneng Company, is not a shareholder of Changchun Zhongtian Company. According to Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law, where a company provides a guarantee to a shareholder or actual controller of the company, it must be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. Therefore, when entering into a guarantee contract, Zhongmin Company should have reviewed whether the person signing the contract had obtained legal authorization and whether the guarantee contract had been approved by a shareholders' meeting resolution of Changchun Zhongtian Company. In this case, Changchun Zhongtian Company did not pass a corresponding shareholders' meeting resolution for this purpose, and Zhongmin Company also failed to provide evidence proving that it had reviewed the shareholders' meeting resolution of Changchun Zhongtian Company consenting to the guarantee. Consequently, the guarantee contract signed by Changchun Zhongtian Company constituted an ultra vires act by its legal representative, and Zhongmin Company should have known that the act of signing this contract exceeded the authority yet still entered into the guarantee contract. Thus, Zhongmin Company is not a bona fide counterparty, and the contract entered into should be deemed invalid according to law. The second-instance judgment's determination that Zhongmin Company, based on the board of directors' resolution of Changchun Zhongtian Company, entered into the Repurchase Agreement and had fulfilled its duty of bona fide review, and that the nature of the agreement should be valid, is indeed improper, and this Court corrects it. The guarantee contract is invalid, and both Changchun Zhongtian Company and Zhongmin Company bear responsibility. According to Article 7 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, effective at that time, which provides that "where the principal contract is valid but the guarantee contract is invalid, if the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the economic losses of the creditor under the principal contract; if both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor cannot repay," Changchun Zhongtian Company shall bear liability for compensation not exceeding one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor cannot repay. Given that Changchun Zhongtian Company's obligation in this case is a repurchase obligation, after it bears the compensation liability, the corresponding lease receivables shall be transferred to Changchun Zhongtian Company.

In summary, the retrial request of Wuhan Zhongneng Gas Co., Ltd. cannot be upheld and shall be dismissed; the retrial request of Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. is partially sustained. Pursuant to Article 214, paragraph 1, and Article 177, paragraph 1, items 1 and 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment of Tianjin High People's Court (2020) Jin Min Zhong No. 370 is reversed.

2. Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 of the Civil Judgment of the Third Intermediate People's Court of Tianjin (2019) Jin 03 Min Chu No. 148 are affirmed.

3. Item 7 of the Civil Judgment of the Third Intermediate People's Court of Tianjin (2019) Jin 03 Min Chu No. 148 is reversed.

4. Item 5 of the Civil Judgment of the Third Intermediate People's Court of Tianjin (2019) Jin 03 Min Chu No. 148 is amended as follows: After the performance of the above payment obligations, if Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. still has part of its claims unsatisfied, Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. shall bear liability for compensation for one-half of the unsatisfied portion. After Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. bears the compensation liability, the corresponding lease receivables shall be transferred to and owned by Zhongxing Tianheng Energy Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.

5. The other claims of Zhongmin International Financial Leasing Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the pecuniary obligation is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
